claim: The non-referential lunch-colleague reading requires variation across occasions.
evidence_summary: In a completed twelve-Friday placement I usually had lunch with a colleague. I ate alone twice. On the other ten Fridays an independent draw assigned the partner, I followed the draw, and all ten draws selected Jo. Constructed.
finding: Changing a draw would have changed my partner. A standing appointment with Jo would have survived that change. The procedure establishes dependence despite identical outcomes. Even in that history the speaker could mean Jo specifically.
proposed_wording: A partner can be determined afresh on each occasion even when every assignment selects the same colleague. Variation across lunches makes this reading easier to distinguish from fixed reference.
inference: Must a partner assigned per occasion ever differ across the occasions that actually occur?

evidence.passage: §8.3, p. 406, [13iii], I usually have lunch with a colleague. The explanation says “in the non-referential case there is variation between one occasion and another”.
